Schütz (eds), Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 1 (Pacific Linguistics A-15), 1-26. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. DOI 10.15144/PL-A15.1 (open edition, CC BY-SA 4.0).
catalog_locator: p. 2, section 2 'Wordlists', spelling note (3); the Varise column is in Section I 'Dialects of Choiseul', pp. 3-6 (accented Varise forms: item 16 'come' (lá)ma p. 3, item 54 'mountain' kúbolo p. 5) pages 2, 3, 4, 5 read as images.
catalog_quote: The only points of spelling that need to be referred to are: (1) the plosives ḅ and ḍ are always prenasalised, except in Kia; (2) g is a velar fricative /γ/ while (3) stress is very frequently ante-penultimate. Any stress that would cause difficulty in interpretation will be marked by an acute accent as in some of the language names above.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (PL A-15 open edition, CC BY-SA, 28 pp.) and rendered p. 2 (PDF page 2) to an image. The passage is there exactly as quoted: 'The only points of spelling that need to be referred to are: (1) the plosives b and d are always prenasalised, except in Kia; (2) g is a velar fricative /γ/ while (3) stress is very frequently ante-penultimate. Any stress that would cause difficulty in interpretation will be marked by an acute accent as in some of the language names above.' Only difference from print: b and d carry a subscript dot in the original (the scanned garbles them as '1' and '9'); wording is identical. Context: it is the transcription note for ALL the wordlists that follow (Section I '…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In the Choiseul languages as transcribed in Capell's wordlists (Babatana, Varisi, Vaghua, Ririo, Sisingga, Kuboro, plus Kia), stress falls on the antepenultimate syllable in most words; deviations are marked with an acute accent in the lists.
new_statements.exceptions: Implied: forms where stress is not antepenultimate are to be marked with an acute accent; no Varisi example is given and no accented Varisi forms survive in the scanned text.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level remark for the whole Choiseul wordlist corpus (lists compiled by Goldie College students), not a Varisi-specific analysis; citation forms in a 100-item Swadesh list; word level.
new_statements.identity_note: Capell 1968 covers the Choiseul languages collectively; the Varisi column is labelled 'Varise' (= vari1239; Tryon & Hackman 1983 list Varese, Ghone, Kiposaka, Uaresi, Vasenggasengga as Varisi communalect names). Ray 1926 pp. 568-571 'Grammar of the Bambatana language (1)' is, per the SMG bibliography, actually Varisi (Kiposaka data), but it contains no stress statement.
